chunks: 1240 - ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Ḥasanī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the hadith that people narrate from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that he said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, descends every Friday night to the lowest heaven?

So he عليه السلام said: May Allah curse those who distort words from their proper places. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not say that. Rather, he عليه السلام said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends down an angel to the lowest heaven every night in the last third, and on the night of al-Jumuʿah at the beginning of the night. Then He commands him, and he calls out: Is there any supplicant so I may give him? Is there any repentant one so I may accept his repentance? Is there any seeker of forgiveness so I may forgive him? O seeker of good, come forward; and O seeker of evil, desist. He continues calling out this until dawn rises; then when dawn rises, he returns to his place from the dominion of heaven.
My father narrated that to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers, from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ الْأَخِيرِ: the last third of the night, a special time of divine mercy
key_terms.الْمُحَرِّفِينَ: those who alter or distort transmitted wording from its proper meaning or place
key_terms.تَائِبٍ: one who repents and turns back to Allah
key_terms.مَلَكًا: an angel commissioned to proclaim the divine call
key_terms.مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاءِ: the celestial dominion or unseen kingdom of heaven
key_terms.يُنْزِلُ: sends down; here, referring to Allah sending an angel, not descending Himself

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith mean that Allah literally descends to the lowest heaven on Friday night?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the attribution of bodily descent to Allah, clarifying instead that Allah sends an angel to the lowest heaven at special times in the night. It emphasizes correct transmission of hadith and highlights divine mercy through the calls to supplication, tawbah, and seeking forgiveness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1240 - Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmoud, who said:
“I said to Imam al-Ridha (as), "O’ son of the Messenger of Allah (sw), what do you say about the narration that people relate from the Messenger of Allah (sw), that Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, descends to the sky of the world every Jumu’ah night?"
Imam (as) replied: "May Allah (swt) curse those who distort words from their proper places. By Allah (swt), the Messenger of Allah (sw) did not say that. What he did say was:
'Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, sends an angel to the sky of the world every night during the last third of the night, and on the night of Jumu’ah at the beginning of the night.
He commands the angel to call out: Is there anyone who asks that I may grant him? Is there anyone who repents so that I may accept his repentance? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness so that I may forgive him? O’ seeker of good, come forward, and O’ seeker of evil, desist.'
The angel continues to call out until the break of dawn, and when dawn breaks, he returns to his place in the celestial realm."
My father narrated this to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers, from the Messenger of Allah (sw).
